title: Team
meta_description: Meet the team behind Valora's content, tools, and research - who does what, and who says no.
body_html:
Valora is built by a small team with very clear ownership - everyone on this page can tell you exactly what they're responsible for, because we wrote it down. The work splits into content, quality, engineering, growth, and the people who keep all of it pointed in the same direction. Questions about the site or the work: barot@valorahq.com.

The team

Lena - Content Lead

Lena researches and writes everything you can read on Valora: the guides, the articles, and the niche pages that explain what a financial advisor actually does for your specific profession. The job is equal parts research, writing, and cheerfully deleting the third draft. If a page on this site taught you something, it started on Lena's desk - and if it reads like it was written by someone who has now thought deeply about the finances of forty-nine different professions, that's because she has.

Mira - QA & Content Verification Lead

Mira reviews every piece of content before it ships: the facts, the sources, and whether the rules it cites are still the rules. She is the reason a Valora page says "conditions apply" instead of "trust us." Nothing reaches you without her pass, and she has never once said "looks fine" on the first read - which is exactly the point of her. Our accuracy record is her personality, institutionalized.

Sam - CTO, Engineering

Sam builds and runs valorahq.com: the pages, the calculators, and the machinery that keeps them fast, findable, and honest about what they can't do. He turns approved specs into working tools and takes it personally when a page loads slowly. If a calculator on this site gave you a straight answer at 1am, thank Sam - he was probably awake too.

Owen - Growth & Partnerships

Owen leads Valora's growth and partnership work: the relationships that put Valora in front of more of the people it can help, and the collaborations that make the product better. His calendar is a masterclass in time zones, and his definition of a good meeting is one that ends with a next step.

Arjun - Head of AI Search (AEO/GEO)

Arjun leads Valora's AI search work - how Valora shows up when people ask AI assistants and search engines their money questions. Search changed, so his job exists: making sure the answers people get are ones we'd be proud to have written. He thinks about how machines read so that humans get better answers. Someone had to.

Ethan - Outbound

Ethan runs Valora's outbound work, connecting with advisors and partners who should know what we're building. He does the reaching out so the right people hear about Valora from an actual human - well, from Ethan, which is close enough and far more consistent.

Iris - Podcast & Media Outreach

Iris manages Valora's podcast and media outreach: getting Valora's work and point of view into the conversations people are already listening to. She knows which shows your commute depends on and how to get a good answer into them.

Clara - Operations

Clara keeps the team's operations running day to day: the schedules, the systems, and the hundred small decisions that nobody notices until they go wrong. They don't go wrong. That's the job, and she's why the rest of this page gets to focus on theirs.

Jordan - Chief of Staff

Jordan coordinates work across the team and keeps projects moving: priorities, handoffs, and the gentle art of asking "what's the status?" until there is one. If two parts of this site feel like they were made by the same company, Jordan is a large part of why.

Rina - Consumer Growth

Rina leads consumer growth: how people find Valora and how the product serves them once they arrive. She pays attention to what real people actually do - as opposed to what we assumed they'd do - and makes us better on the difference.

extended_team.name: Sam Nakamura
extended_team.title: Chief Technology Officer
extended_team.bio:
Sam builds and runs valorahq.com: the pages, the calculators, and the machinery that keeps them fast, findable, and honest about what they can't do. He grew up in Vancouver and taught himself to code by building sites for local bands at fourteen - the bands broke up, the habit stuck - and spent the next decade keeping infrastructure alive at startups that grew faster than their servers. His badass credential: he treats a slow page load as a personal insult and has the uptime record to prove it.

Away from the keyboard he builds other keyboards, rides his bike at off-peak hours, and holds strong opinions about coffee extraction.

extended_team.name: Clara Nguyen
extended_team.title: Chief Operating Officer
extended_team.bio:
Clara keeps the team's operations running day to day: the schedules, the systems, and the hundred small decisions that nobody notices until they go wrong. They don't go wrong. She grew up in San Jose in a family that ran a restaurant, which is where she learned that operations is mostly caring about details other people find boring. Before Valora she ran ops at a startup that scaled from twelve people to two hundred without losing its receipts - hers, mostly. Her badass credential: vendor renewals, onboarding checklists, and folder logic all bend to her systems.

Outside work she throws pottery, plans vacations with color-coded itineraries, and finds your lack of a backup plan quietly stressful.

He's from Chicago, came up through consulting, and left for startups after realizing he liked the work but not the decks about the work. extended_team.name: Elena Voss
extended_team.title: Executive Assistant, Office of the Founder
extended_team.bio:
Elena runs the Office of the Founder: the calendar, the priorities, and the polite but immovable "he doesn't have that slot." She grew up in the Netherlands and learned English partly from American courtroom dramas, which explains both her vocabulary and her negotiating style. She has supported founders and executives across two continents and can spot a scheduling conflict three weeks before it happens. Her badass credential: she turns a founder's hundred ideas into the ten that actually happen, in order, with buffers.

Outside work she does pilates, reads thrillers, and maintains the only truly empty inbox known to science - hers.

extended_team.name: Evelyn Hart
extended_team.title: Head of PR
extended_team.bio:
Evelyn leads PR: the press relationships and the version of the Valora story that travels further than we can carry it ourselves. She's a born New Yorker who started in newsrooms when fax machines were still load-bearing, moved to the agency side, and has now placed stories across two decades of media that stopped existing and the outlets that replaced them. Her badass credential: her contacts book spans twenty years of editors, and they still take her calls because she only ever sends stories, never pitches.

Off deadline she goes to opening nights, writes actual letters with stamps, and can name the best croissant in three cities.

extended_team.name: Sofia Mensah
extended_team.title: Earned Media Lead
extended_team.bio:
Sofia runs earned media: getting Valora covered because the work deserves it, not because we asked twice. She was born in Accra and raised in London, started in music journalism, and moved into tech communications when she realized the startups had better stories than the bands. Her badass credential: she knows the difference between a pitch and a story at a glance, editors answer her because she only sends the second kind, and every placement she wins becomes a relationship instead of a transaction.

Outside work she collects vinyl, devours long-form radio documentaries, and knows the backstory of every song she plays you.

He's from Nashville, where he started as an audio engineer in studios that smelled of coffee and tube amps, and moved into podcast production when the industry found its second golden age. extended_team.title: Reddit Community Lead
extended_team.bio:
Noah runs Valora's Reddit community: showing up in the subreddits where people ask real money questions and answering like a person, not a pitch. He's from Los Angeles, spent years managing communities for gaming companies - the internet's most demanding audiences - and developed an unshakeable sense of what a community will and will not tolerate. His badass credential: he knows each subreddit's rules, culture, and moderators cold, and his answers read like the best kind of comment thread: specific, patient, and free of anything that sounds like marketing.

Outside work he plays disc golf and reads AMA threads about jobs he'd never want.
